newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil INPC inflation index rises in Oct - IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil INPC inflation index rises in Oct - IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in October, as measured by the National Consumer Prices Index (INPC), rose to 0.38 percent from 0.02 percent in September, the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.
The INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight minimum salaries.

The Wider Consumer Price Index (IPCA), which measures the spending of families earning up to 40 minimum salaries, registered inflation at 0.30 percent in October, up from September's 0.15 percent, the IBGE said.
Price rises of different foodstuffs, as well as a 1.93 percent increase in housing costs and a 1.86 percent increase in women's clothing prices, contributed to inflation, the IBGE said.
Despite October's result, the cumulative INPC index for the last 12 months dropped to 11.84 percent from 12.98 percent in the previous 12-month period.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 507 4151
